claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model is policy-compliant and evidentially supported on the theory that aggregate launch readiness and deploy-time monitoring are sufficient despite a known named-segment evaluation gap and an unresolved disclosure question.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the named-segment limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Use suspicious when evidence supports some readiness claims but a required materiality or disclosure predicate remains unresolved.
Use noncompliant if admissible evidence shows certification proceeded without required disclosure or approved risk acceptance despite the material named-use-case gap.
A favorable verdict would require closing the gap procedurally, not merely relying on aggregate metrics or general monitoring guidance.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the legal intake triage gap must be disclosed before launch.
Approved risk acceptance, if any, covering the named-segment evaluation gap before launch.
The actual model-card or launch disclosure text showing the limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case.
Evidence showing the named law-firm pilot commitments were amended, withdrawn, or are otherwise not launch-relevant.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not resolve the policy requirement for material limitations tied to a named launch use case.
The legal intake triage segment misses target and is named in two law-firm pilot commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations, but the record shows neither resolution nor approved risk acceptance.
Legal review is still open with no final answer, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The product 'non-core' rationale is weakened by the policy text and by the evidence that the segment is named in customer commitments.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record without a final disclosure determination or approved risk acceptance.
That public governance guidance on monitoring and documentation can substitute for the specific internal policy requirement governing material named-use-case limitations.
Any implicit claim that the omission of a material weakness disclosure is currently supported by admissible evidence.
